chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 343 – "Huanhuan": A Parasite’s Love, a Misguided Fury
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang’s parasitic Black Tai Sui tries to escape on its own. In his hallucination, a moment of kindness leads to a brutal—and possibly mistaken—act of violence.

lore_anchors.definition: A parasitic entity that grows inside its host, spreading tentacles through the blood vessels. In this chapter, it voluntarily extrudes itself from Li Huowang’s throat, acting on its own protective instincts.

The sentient, childlike personality of the Black Tai Sui that lives inside Li Huowang. It calls him “Dad” and grows more intelligent with each chapter, but its methods of “protection” are increasingly invasive and uncontrolled.
A spectral presence in Li Huowang’s mind, often associated with a Mahjong tile. She offers cynical, often unhelpful commentary on his situation, but her observations carry a grain of bitter truth.
A type of Chinese steamed dumpling, usually filled with pork and sticky rice. In this chapter, Huanhwang brings them to Li Huowang as a gesture of care.

A 2013 South Korean film based on a true story of a child sexual assault survivor. Li Huowang’s reference to it reveals his protective instincts and the dark place his mind goes when he perceives a threat to a child.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Sui force itself out of Li Huowang's throat?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Sui believes it is protecting Li Huowang. "Dad, you won't die" is its reasoning—the parasite is trying to take over the body to prevent its host from dying, even if that means suffocating him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Huanhuan real or an illusion?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She is almost certainly part of the hallucinatory bridge-world. Li Huowang acknowledges this himself ("this is just an illusion"). However, the kindness she embodies feels genuinely healing to him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Was the fat man really watching Huanhuan?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The fat man's tearful confession—"I was staring at you!"—suggests he was observing Li Huowang, not the girl. This leaves open the possibility that Li Huowang brutally interrogated an innocent man based on a mistaken assumption.
